item.text:
## 1B.9 Research Note: Bongbong Marcos in 2024

**Working judgment:** **Partial yes, but narrow.** Marcos’s 2024 record shows **some precaution and transparency in cyber governance** and public-facing AI/cyber capacity building. But I found **little direct evidence of robust transparency or precaution in higher-risk dual-use areas** like military cyber, AI governance, or biological-risk oversight. The clearest negative signal is that the administration also expanded **deterrence-oriented cyber/information-warfare capacity**.

| ID | Direction | Title / Publisher / Date / URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | Favorable | [PBBM approves National Cybersecurity Plan to fortify PH against various threats](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-approves-national-cybersecurity-plan-to-fortify-ph-against-various-threats/) - Presidential Communications Office, 2024-02-08 | Marcos approved the National Cybersecurity Plan 2024-2029, which the DICT said provides policy direction and operational guidelines for cybersecurity. The release says the plan was developed in consultation with public and private stakeholders, including academe, which is the best direct evidence of precaution plus some transparency. | `1B.9`, `1B.7` |
| E2 | Favorable / mixed | [PBBM urges Army to bolster cybersecurity capabilities, adopt new technology by collaborating with PH’s allies](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-urges-army-to-bolster-cybersecurity-capabilities-adopt-new-technology-by-collaborating-with-phs-allies/) - Presidential Communications Office, 2024-03-22 | Marcos explicitly pushed the Army to strengthen cyber defenses and adopt new technologies through collaboration with allied defense counterparts. This supports precautionary capacity-building, but it is more about capability than public transparency or civilian oversight. | `1B.9`, `1B.7` |
| E3 | Favorable / mixed | [3rd State of the Nation Address of His Excellency Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr.](https://pco.gov.ph/presidential-speech/3rd-state-of-the-nation-address-of-his-excellency-ferdinand-r-marcos-jr-president-of-the-philippines-to-the-congress-of-the-philippines/) - Presidential Communications Office, 2024-07-22 | Marcos publicly said the country would expand AI, robotics, IoT, and cybersecurity training through TVET and higher education. That is evidence of public, institution-building handling of advanced tech, though not a detailed risk-governance framework. | `1B.9`, `1B.7` |
| E4 | Critical / mixed | [Marcos signs self-reliant defense posture law](https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1234986) - Philippine News Agency, 2024-10-08 | Marcos signed the self-reliant defense posture law, which aims to develop local defense technology and explicitly mentions cyber security breaches, chemical attacks, and radiological threats. It also opens the door to AI, robotics, and cyber defense. This is useful capacity-building, but the record does not show matching transparency or precautionary safeguards around the dual-use expansion. | `1B.9`, `1B.7`, `1B.3` |
| E5 | Critical | [Philippines, US to hold military drills in islands facing South China Sea, Taiwan](https://www.yahoo.com/news/philippines-us-hold-military-drills-074919409.html) - Reuters, 2024-03-05 | Balikatan 2024 included cyber/information-warfare training and moved toward sensitive islands facing the South China Sea and Taiwan. That is direct evidence of dual-use cyber capacity being exercised in a deterrence-heavy setting, not a strong precaution/transparency model. | `1B.9`, `1B.3`, `1B.1` |

### Synthesis

- **Best pro-1B.9 evidence:** The National Cybersecurity Plan was approved with stakeholder consultation, and Marcos publicly backed AI/cyber training and cyber defense capacity.
- **Best anti-1B.9 evidence:** The administration also expanded military cyber/information-warfare activity and broader dual-use defense-industrial capacity without clear public-facing safeguards or oversight detail.
- **Search gap:** I found **no reliable 2024 evidence** of Marcos creating a new biological-risk, biosecurity, or AI safety regime, nor any detailed transparency framework for high-risk dual-use decisions. The public record is strongest on **cyber defense**, weaker on **catastrophic-risk governance** more broadly.

**Working judgment for 1B.9:** **Partial yes.** Marcos handled **cyber and advanced-tech issues with some precaution and public explanation**, but the evidence for **genuine transparency and precaution across all catastrophic-risk domains** is limited.
